method: Read every current JP row from cities.json and join each ID to JP.txt in raw/JP.zip. Crosscheck GeoNames admin2 ID and admin2Codes.txt labels.

Read all 47 publicly available J-LIS prefecture municipality/code lists. The retrieved pages contain 1,841 parsed municipality/ward entries; the Hokkaido page output was partial, but every selected Hokkaido city appeared. This audit does not claim exhaustive coverage of all Japanese municipalities.

For each selected city, search official same-prefecture rows against the current name, language-tagged alternatives, and the matched admin2 alternatives. A candidate currentName+市 is a lookup hypothesis only and is accepted only when the full string is present in the official list; no longest-name or blind suffix rule was used.
All 199 city entries have exactly one matched full official municipality name. Tokyo 東京 is an explicit capital/urban-name exception and remains unchanged.

For English, compare diacritic-insensitive romanization of every row with its admin2 label, ignoring legal -shi, spaces/hyphens, and comma qualifiers for comparison only. Review all five discrepancies against municipal government websites. This is identity/name verification, not an exhaustive per-city English-branding style audit.
Check suspicious native alternatives and city-versus-neighborhood mismatches on municipal official websites.

patchPolicy.japan_patches.json: All 172 executable field changes for the requested consistent full official Japanese municipality-name policy. Each correction or consistency change is marked with type.
patchPolicy.japan_definite_patches.json: Five definite field corrections, excluding consistency-only suffix changes.
patchPolicy.japan_suffix_normalization.json: 167 full-municipality-name consistency changes. These original values are valid city stems, not corrupted names.
patchPolicy.japan_all_full_names_patches.json: Alias of the full 172-field executable patch list.

definitePatches.reason: The city government identifies itself as 四日市市. The place-name stem is 四日市; 四日 loses the final 市 in the proper name as well as the municipal suffix.
The city government identifies itself as 市原市; 原 is a truncated alternate that removes meaningful parts of the proper name.
The municipal name is 調布市. 調布ヶ丘/調布ケ丘 denotes an area within the city, not the city as a whole.
Kukichūō (久喜中央) is an address/neighborhood within Kuki. The selected city record must display the municipality Kuki. The city homepage uses KUKI CITY.
The city government uses Tondabayashi City. Tondabayashichō refers to the town/locality form rather than the current municipality; city status dates to 1950.

targetedRetainedNames.decision: Retain Minoh rather than raw ADM2 Minoo. The municipality explicitly standardizes Minoh.
Retain Matsusaka and 松阪 stem. Reject cache 松坂市 and admin2 Matsuzaka-shi as display sources.
Retain 諫 character; do not select cache 諌早市 merely because it is longer.
Retain accepted capital/urban name 東京, not an invented 東京市.
Name is confirmed independently against Kanagawa J-LIS and city website despite anomalous GeoNames Kōza-gun admin2 parent.

adjacentDataWarnings.detail: The current GeoNames parent is Kōza-gun (1858593), rather than Ebina city. The official municipality name is independently confirmed as 海老名市. Current coordinate 35.38121,139.39651 should be checked separately before changing anything; this task did not verify or modify coordinates.

nativeRows.reason: Tokyo is retained as the accepted capital/urban name, rather than inventing Tokyo-shi or forcing the metropolis name.

sourceFreshnessNote: J-LIS lists are official live pages read on the audit date. Their individual displayed update dates vary; no claim is made that each municipality updated its page on 2026-10-07. Targeted municipal sources include current government homepages.
